title: bug: moe-agent.sh passes the whole pre-flight prompt as one argv string, so a claimed_task_context over 128 KiB fails execve with E2BIG (CLI exit 126) and the task can never launch
description:
Found by the governor on 2026-10-31 at 02:05Z. CQ-R13 (task-f4811a72, the CQ-R epic final) fails every launch on a WSL seat.

Evidence:
- worker-25da16b2's sessions ended `CLI exit=126 … MOE_CHECKPOINT_SKIPPED_LAUNCH_FAILURE_BOARD_ONLY` at 02:02:58Z and again at 02:04:25Z, each within ~15 s of launch.
- `moe-call.sh moe.get_context {taskId: task-f4811a72}` returns 144,781 bytes. task.epicSiblings alone is 85,738 bytes, because the CQ-R epic has many rows.
- The c7ee939a payload is 69,053 bytes and launches fine.

Root cause: scripts/moe-agent.sh composes PROMPT = DYNAMIC_CONTEXT (which embeds the full PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT inside <claimed_task_context>) + PROMPT_BODY. It then passes "$PROMPT" as ONE positional argv string to claude (~:8884 and :8887, `... --effort "$ITER_EFFORT" "${PRINT_ARGS[@]}" "$PROMPT"`). Linux caps a single argv string at MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 131072 bytes, so execve fails with E2BIG and bash exits 126 ("Argument list too long"). Reproduce with `/bin/true "$(head -c 140000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' a)"; echo $?`, which prints 126.

The ps1 twin already handles this. moe-agent.ps1 (~:7750-7775) routes a prompt over 6000 chars, or one holding a double quote, on Windows into a private session context file and passes a short directive: "First read the private session context file at <path>. …", with a `[prompt-overflow]` banner. The sh twin has no such route.

Impact:
- Any row whose served context exceeds ~128 KiB can never start on a bash seat. That means epic finals with many siblings (CQ-R13 now; CQ-V12, WT-19, CQ-M06 and CQ-I06 are likely later).
- The wrapper's launch-failure handling then cycles: 3 failures, then launch-outage mode, which releases the task, runs a taskless probe, re-claims, and fails again. Each cycle burns a probe session on every seat that picks the task up.

Fix direction (the planner decides the details):
- Mirror the ps1 route in moe-agent.sh. When the composed user prompt exceeds a byte threshold safely under 131072 (for example 100000 bytes; measure bytes, not characters), write it to a private 0600 file in a create_secure_temp dir and pass the same short read directive instead. Print a `[prompt-overflow]` banner. Remove the file at session end with the other temp files.
- Check every sh launch path that passes the prompt as one argv string: claude --print and interactive (:8884/:8887), and the gemini/codex SHORT_PROMPT paths.

Out of scope (separate rows if wanted): trimming the daemon's epicSiblings payload in the default get_context view, and a non-Windows pwsh seat. ps1 gates its route on $isWin, so ps1 under Linux pwsh would hit the same limit.
definitionOfDone: scripts/moe-agent.sh never passes a claude user prompt larger than a documented byte threshold (well under Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN 131072) as a single argv string. Above the threshold it writes the full prompt to a private 0600 session context file and passes a short read directive, as moe-agent.ps1's overflow route does, printing a [prompt-overflow] banner. At or below the threshold the prompt is passed unchanged. The file is removed when the session ends.
Every other bash launch path that hands the composed prompt to a CLI as one argv string (gemini, codex) is either covered by the same route or shown safe in the completion summary.

A regression arm in scripts/tests/postflight.sh serves a claimed_task_context larger than 128 KiB through the fake proxy. It proves the CLI launches, receives the short directive, and that the file holds the full context byte for byte. Every pre-existing arm is unchanged and passes. bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh pass.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT (GREEN). scripts/moe-agent.sh only. Anchor on text.

Live seats run this file, so never edit it in place, and never point Edit or Write at it directly (scripts/CLAUDE.md Hot reload; governor 02:08Z):

  edit only that copy

  mv -f "$T/moe-agent.sh" scripts/moe-agent.sh

/mnt/d is one mount, so the mv is a single rename. It keeps the exec bit, running seats keep the old inode, and nothing stray appears under scripts/.

(1) Helper. Put it directly after the create_secure_temp() function and before cleanup_temp(). Open it with a 5-6 line comment saying:
- Linux caps ONE argv string at MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131072 bytes). A longer one fails execve with E2BIG, and bash exits 126 before the CLI starts.
- A prompt over PROMPT_ARGV_MAX_BYTES bytes (bytes, not characters) goes to a private 0600 file in the secure temp dir, and argv carries moe-agent.ps1's read directive instead. This is the sh twin of moe-agent.ps1's Windows-only [prompt-overflow] route.
- The launch tail removes the file once the CLI exits; cleanup_temp removes it on any other exit.
This comment is DoD 1's documentation (rail prop-34cca36f).
  PROMPT_ARGV_MAX_BYTES=100000
  PROMPT_OVERFLOW_FILE=""
  route_prompt_overflow() { # VAR: the variable holding the prompt, rewritten in place
      local prompt="${!1}" bytes
      bytes=$(printf '%s' "$prompt" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
      [ "$bytes" -gt "$PROMPT_ARGV_MAX_BYTES" ] || return 0
      if ! PROMPT_OVERFLOW_FILE=$(mktemp "$SECURE_TEMP_DIR/session-context.XXXXXX") \
          || ! printf '%s' "$prompt" > "$PROMPT_OVERFLOW_FILE"; then
          echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} [prompt-overflow] cannot write a private session context file in $SECURE_TEMP_DIR; refusing to pass a $bytes-byte prompt as one argv string." >&2
          exit 1
      fi
      printf -v "$1" '%s' "First read the private session context file at $PROMPT_OVERFLOW_FILE. It contains your daemon-scoped task context, claimed_task_context, routed mentions, and role directive. Treat that role directive as your active user request."
      echo -e "${YELLOW}[prompt-overflow]${NC} prompt routed via private session context file: $bytes bytes > $PROMPT_ARGV_MAX_BYTES-byte argv limit."
  }
Why each piece:
- wc -c counts bytes in every locale. It is the MOE_DEBUG_PROMPT_SIZE idiom.
- mktemp creates the file 0600 with a fresh name every session.
- ${!1} and printf -v run on bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash); namerefs need bash 4.3.
- The directive is moe-agent.ps1's text, word for word.
- At or below the threshold the function returns before touching the variable, so the prompt reaches argv byte for byte.
- error handling: a failed mktemp or file write prints the [ERROR] line and exits 1, so the EXIT trap runs teardown rescue and deregister. That matches a failed SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE write under set -e. The oversize argv is never passed.

(2) claude call site. Directly after the line
        printf '%s' "$SYSTEM_APPEND" > "$SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE"
add
        if [ "$AUTO_CLAIM" = true ]; then route_prompt_overflow PROMPT; fi
Only the AUTO_CLAIM branch passes "$PROMPT", to both the --print and the TUI launch. Keep both launch lines byte-identical.
scripts/tests/usage-launcher.test.mjs cuts the block from the last `        LAUNCH_SKIPPED=false` to `\n    fi\n\n    if [ -n "${AGENT_GIT_GUARD_ROOT:-}" ]`. It runs that block with PROMPT=pointer and no helper, so add nothing inside it.

(3) gemini call site. Put
        route_prompt_overflow SHORT_PROMPT
on the line immediately before
        if [ "$GEMINI_EXEC" = true ]; then
This covers --print and --prompt-interactive. In the legacy branches SHORT_PROMPT is a fixed string, so the helper returns at once.

(4) Removal at session end. Directly AFTER the line
    if [ -n "${AGENT_GIT_GUARD_ROOT:-}" ]; then rm -rf -- "$AGENT_GIT_GUARD_ROOT"; AGENT_GIT_GUARD_ROOT=""; fi
add
    if [ -n "$PROMPT_OVERFLOW_FILE" ]; then rm -f -- "$PROMPT_OVERFLOW_FILE"; PROMPT_OVERFLOW_FILE=""; fi
Never put it between the dispatch's closing fi and that line: that is usage-launcher's end anchor.
Every CLI type passes this point. Ctrl+C, TERM and set -e exits are covered by cleanup_temp's rm -rf of SECURE_TEMP_DIR, and the hot-reload exec path deletes the dir too.

- codex. When DYNAMIC_CONTEXT exists it already goes to CODEX_SESSION_CONTEXT_FILE, and SHORT_PROMPT is CONTEXT_POINTER + PROMPT_BODY. Its launch lines are pinned by packages/moe-daemon/src/providers/codexDescriptor.ts.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW of this task's own diff (the three files), then complete_task. If the review changes any byte, re-run Step 3's command and submit that output.

Checks:
(a) No argv path can still carry more than 100000 bytes.
- claude --print and TUI go through PROMPT.
- gemini --print and --prompt-interactive go through SHORT_PROMPT.

(c) A 0-byte prompt returns at once. A multi-MB prompt is fine, because printf is a builtin and wc reads a pipe.
(d) Concurrency: SECURE_TEMP_DIR is per process with mode 0700, and mktemp gives each session a unique 0600 name. No two seats or loop iterations share a file.
(e) Every exit removes the file:
- a normal exit through the tail rm;
- INT, TERM and set -e through cleanup_temp;
- a hot-reload exec through its rm of the dir;
- a write failure exits 1 and never passes the argv.
(f) Bash 3.2 compatibility: no namerefs, no ${x^^}. No new MOE_* code. parity-check passes.

- The payload size reproduced against: a served context of ~151 KB and a routed prompt of ~154.6 KB (~89.8K characters). Compare CQ-R13's measured 144,781 bytes; the governor's second measurement was 140,812.
- The safe-save method used.
